claim: For the real two-dimensional Lorentz sequence space \(X=d^{(2)}(w,2)\) with weights \(w_1\ge w_2>0\), put \(a=w_2/w_1\). Then \(d_{\mathrm{BM}}(X,\ell_2^2)^2=C_{\mathrm{NJ}}(X)=C_{\mathrm{Pt}}(X)=2/(1+a)=2w_1/(w_1+w_2)\).
integrity: All three equalities are supported by explicit two-sided arguments. The Banach-Mazur lower bound quantifies over arbitrary ellipses; the Jordan-von Neumann and Ptolemy lower bounds use explicit extremizing configurations. Uninspected literature is recorded as residual risk rather than treated as noncoverage.
scientific_limitations: The theorem is restricted to real two-dimensional Lorentz sequence spaces with exponent q=2. A 2006 tensor-product paper mentioning Banach-Mazur distances and Lorentz sequence spaces could not be inspected in full and remains a literature-coverage risk.
title: Euclidean distortion, Jordan--von Neumann, and Ptolemy constants coincide on the \(q=2\) Lorentz plane
